stem.en: Anil's taxable income rises from ₹16,00,000 to ₹16,10,000, so part of it now falls in the 20% slab. What happens to his income tax?

text.en: It rises by ₹3,22,000, because 20% is now charged on the whole ₹16,10,000.
It rises by ₹2,000, because only the extra ₹10,000 is taxed at 20%.
It stays the same, because the standard deduction grows with every raise.
It falls, because the 15% slab no longer applies to any part of his income.

explanation.en: Each slab charges its own rate on the part of the income inside it. At ₹16,00,000 the tax is ₹20,000 + ₹40,000 + ₹60,000 = ₹1,20,000. At ₹16,10,000 the same ₹1,20,000 is due, plus 20% of the extra ₹10,000, which is ₹2,000. So the tax rises by ₹2,000 and he keeps ₹8,000 of the raise.

hints.en: Work out the tax at ₹16,00,000 slab by slab, then add the tax on the extra ₹10,000.
Only the part above ₹16,00,000 is in the 20% slab.
